name: Cluster networking
summary: The very fast network that lets thousands of accelerators share results every training step, so the whole cluster behaves like one computer.

D1.guide: Predict: if one cable is slow, how many chips end up waiting?
text: When thousands of chips learn together, they must keep sharing notes, many times a second.
So they are joined by super fast cables, like a team passing a ball. If one pass is slow, the whole team waits.
D1.analogy: A team passing a ball: one slow pass holds everyone up.

text: Inside one server, accelerators talk over a very fast local link. Between servers, a **fabric** of switches connects them, usually **InfiniBand** or high-speed **Ethernet** with RDMA, which moves data straight between memories without the CPU in the way.
After each training step, every accelerator must combine its results with all the others (a **collective** such as all-reduce). The step can't finish until the slowest transfer does.
That is why people say the network is the computer: adding chips only helps if the network can keep them fed, and network layout decides which jobs can run where.

D2.analogy: A team passing a ball: one slow pass holds everyone up.
D2.analogyBreaks: A team can improvise around a dropped pass. A synchronised collective can't: one faulty link or congested switch slows every chip in the job, and finding which of thousands of links is to blame is hard.

predict.question: A cluster doubles its GPUs but keeps the same network. What usually happens to training speed?
options: It rises by less than double, because chips spend more time waiting on the network
predict.explanation: More chips means more data to exchange each step. If the network doesn't grow too, the extra chips spend part of their time waiting.

text: Open problems: training across several data centres where links are slower, keeping huge fabrics free of congestion, and spotting failing links before they stall a job.
InfiniBand and Ethernet compete for AI clusters, and industry groups are extending Ethernet for this workload.
